description:
This image provides a panoramic view looking out over the Strait of Gibraltar from the Pillars of Hercules viewpoint.

*   **Orientation/Heading:** The viewpoint appears to be generally facing south-southeast, looking across the strait towards the distant coast of Africa (or possibly the Spanish coast further east).
*   **Visible:**
    *   **Foreground (right):** A green coin-operated telescope on a black railing is prominently visible.
    *   **Midground (center to left):** The deep blue waters of the Strait of Gibraltar are visible, dotted with numerous cargo ships and tankers at anchor or in transit. Below the viewpoint, some buildings and roads are nestled amidst lush green Mediterranean vegetation.
    *   **Background:** A hazy coastline with mountains rises in the distance, likely representing the coast of North Africa (Morocco) or the Spanish mainland. A clear blue sky with a few wispy clouds dominates the upper portion of the image.
*   **Occluded:** The immediate ground directly beneath the viewpoint is mostly occluded by the railing and vegetation. The full extent of Gibraltar's rock behind the viewer is also not visible.

highlights.text: In 711 AD, Tariq ibn Ziyad led an army of around 7,000 soldiers across the strait from North Africa, initiating the Umayyad conquest of Hispania.
Jebel Musa in Morocco represents the southern Pillar of Hercules, matching the Rock of Gibraltar to the north in ancient Greek mythology.
The landing spot at the foot of the Rock was named 'Jebel Tariq' (Mountain of Tariq) in honor of the commander, which eventually evolved into the name 'Gibraltar'.
